data.title: Western Digital stock rises as strong earnings offset capex and supply concerns
data.description:
Western Digital WDC reported strong fiscal first-quarter results and issued an upbeat outlook as demand for hard disk drives (HDDs) continued to benefit from artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.

However, concerns about rising capital expenditure, potential increases in industry supply, and the sustainability of demand prompted mixed reactions from Wall Street analysts.

The company’s revenue rose 55% year over year to $4.38 billion, beating analyst expectations of $4.14 billion, while adjusted earnings per share reached $4.64, above consensus estimates.

Western Digital shares rose 1.06% on Friday.

The stock had more than doubled in value during the year through Thursday’s close, leaving investors to weigh the company’s strong operating performance against its valuation.

Analysts split over Western Digital’s valuation outlook

Morgan Stanley raised its price target on Western Digital to $668 from $643 and maintained an Overweight rating.

The firm described the results as a “strong, pricing-driven beat” and highlighted the company’s robust guidance for the December quarter.

However, Morgan Stanley also cautioned that “the market continues to be fickle".

UBS took a more cautious stance, lowering its price target to $435 from $470 while retaining a Neutral rating.

The firm acknowledged strong results and demand constrained by supply but warned that higher capital expenditure, accelerating industry supply and uncertainty about demand beyond the current cycle could put further pressure on the stock’s valuation.

Citi maintained its Buy rating, saying the results reinforced its positive outlook for the HDD storage cycle.

However, it lowered its price target because of a reduced valuation multiple for comparable companies.

Goldman Sachs also flagged valuation risks.

The firm said the shares could trade modestly lower despite strong results and guidance above consensus, citing elevated near-term capital expenditure and the possibility of competitors increasing capacity.

AI infrastructure supports demand and pricing

Western Digital’s results reflect continued demand for data storage linked to the expansion of AI infrastructure.

Chief Executive Irving Tan told analysts on Thursday that demand for the company’s HDDs remained strong and was increasingly coming from customers outside its traditional base, including neocloud providers and AI frontier labs.

The company’s blended average selling price per terabyte of storage increased 28% during the first quarter, indicating stronger pricing alongside higher revenue.

Tan said the company’s visibility into demand was extending further.

He added that Western Digital had visibility through 2030 or 2031 across its seven largest customers.

The outlook suggests that demand could remain supportive over the coming years, although analysts differ on how much of that potential is already reflected in the share price.

Strong second-quarter guidance and higher dividend

Western Digital expects fiscal second-quarter revenue of $5 billion to $5.2 billion, representing approximately 69% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.

It forecasts an adjusted gross margin of 60% to 61% and adjusted earnings per share of $5.60 to $6.

The company reported first-quarter profit of $1.78 billion, or $4.63 per share, compared with $1.15 billion, or $3.07 per share, a year earlier.

Western Digital also increased its quarterly dividend by 17% to 17.5 cents per share. The dividend is payable on December 17 to shareholders of record as of December 4.

The strong results and outlook underline the benefits of rising storage demand, but concerns over investment spending, competitive supply, and valuation continue to divide analysts.

data.title: These airline stocks remain worth owning despite $100 oil
data.description:
Oil’s return above $100 a barrel has made airline investing a tougher proposition.

As of writing, US crude sits comfortably above $100 while Brent is hovering around $114 as Middle East supply concerns intensify.

For air carriers, the challenge extends beyond crude – jet fuel prices and the ability to recover costs through fares ultimately determine profitability.

Against the current backdrop, Delta Air Lines, Ryanair, and United Airlines remain worth owning heading into 2027. Here’s what makes these airline stocks attractive despite elevated oil prices.

Delta Air Lines: a refinery provides an unusual buffer

Delta Air Lines offers something most airline stocks cannot – a refinery business that can partially offset the cost of turning crude into aviation fuel.

Its December-quarter outlook incorporates a refinery benefit of about 40 cents per gallon, bringing projected all-in fuel costs to about $4.25.

That provides a tangible cushion when jet fuel becomes particularly expensive relative to crude.

The September quarter demonstrated resilience. DAL generated $1.72 in adjusted earnings a share and a 9.4% adjusted operating margin.

Management still projects roughly $2.5 billion in full-year free cash flow.

That combination makes Delta Air Lines stock a compelling pick – it has both an operating buffer and cash generation to support its finances through the squeeze.

However, the refinery cannot neutralize every increase. Delta reduced its annual adjusted earnings forecast to $5.10–$5.60 per share, underscoring that resilience still comes with pressure on profits.

United Airlines: customers are helping absorb the fuel shock

United Airlines earns its place through demonstrated sales strength across several customer groups.

Q3 revenue increased 17% to a record $17.9 billion, while revenue per available seat mile climbed 16%. Premium revenue rose 17%, contracted business revenue advanced 26%, and cargo revenue increased 23%.

Despite a 62% jump in fuel expense, United delivered adjusted earnings of $2.54 per share, within its guidance.

Those figures support the investment case: UAL has multiple sources of additional revenue to help absorb expensive fuel.

It offers more ways to recover costs than a carrier dependent mostly on filling seats with discounted tickets.

Its outlook also explicitly allows for substantial fuel pressure.

United Airlines projects Q4 adjusted earnings of $0.50–$1.50 per share while assuming fuel costs of approximately $4.80 per gallon.

That leaves it exposed to further increases, but demonstrates a path to profitability under demanding assumptions.

Ryanair: fuel hedges buy valuable breathing room

Ryanair provides the most direct near-term protection of these three picks through its fuel hedges.

The European budget carrier has reported roughly 80% of its jet fuel requirements hedged through March 2027 at around $67 per barrel.

It has also reduced its fiscal-year passenger target to 214 million from 216 million and plans broadly flat winter capacity, limiting exposure to costly unhedged fuel.

That combination is the attraction: contracted fuel protection and a willingness to sacrifice growth when additional flying becomes less attractive.

Against less-hedged competitors, Ryanair has more breathing room to protect profitability.

The investment case becomes harder after March. CEO Michael O’Leary said on October 20 that only 15% of the following year’s fuel costs were secured at $85 per barrel.

He expects sharply higher European fares as industry costs rise.

Investors should therefore treat Ryanair’s current hedge advantage as time to adapt, with future returns depending on pricing and capacity discipline.

data.title: Gold extends losses but UBS sees key support ahead
data.description:
Spot gold prices were little changed in early US trading Friday, holding near levels reached after Thursday’s steep losses.

Spot gold was trading at $4020 an ounce, down 0.1% but silver declined sharply, trading at $54 with the day's loss of just over 1%.

Renewed tensions in the Middle East have driven oil prices higher, adding to inflation concerns and strengthening expectations that the Federal Reserve will keep monetary policy restrictive.

Gold has struggled to draw sustained safe-haven buying despite rising geopolitical risks and weakness in global equities.

Silver has come under additional pressure, with investors weighing the potential impact of high borrowing costs and rising energy prices on industrial activity.

Market sentiment remains shaped by persistent inflation risks and expectations for further monetary tightening.

Interest rate futures suggest the Fed is widely expected to leave rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, while traders continue to price in about a 78% probability of at least one additional rate increase by December.

Firm rate expectations, higher crude prices and continued selling pressure have made it difficult for bullion to benefit from geopolitical uncertainty, even during periods of easing bond yields.

Middle East tensions put gold and silver under pressure

The latest escalation in the Middle East has renewed concerns over the security of energy shipments through the Persian Gulf, despite producers’ efforts to redirect supplies through alternative infrastructure.

Brent crude briefly approached $115 a barrel, its highest level in roughly five months, while West Texas Intermediate rose above $100.

For gold, the conflict has created competing forces.

The risk of further military confrontation and interruptions to energy supplies can support demand for defensive assets. However, higher oil prices also threaten to keep inflation elevated, potentially giving the Fed reason to maintain tighter monetary conditions for longer.

That tension has muted gold’s traditional safe-haven response.

Some investors have instead directed defensive flows toward US government bonds, while rising yields have added to the pressure on non-yielding bullion.

Silver has faced heavier selling as investors consider whether expensive energy and restrictive monetary policy could weigh on manufacturing and industrial demand.

UBS identifies $4,000 as a key support level

Despite the pressure from higher yields, UBS strategist Giovanni Staunovo said gold had shown resilience.

“Still, we think gold has proved notably resilient to the sharp rise in yields,” Staunovo wrote.

UBS expects the metal could face another test of the $4,000-an-ounce level in the near term, with longer-term buyers potentially stepping in if prices retreat further.

“In the near term, gold may retest support around USD 4,000/oz, where we expect structural dip buyers to establish a floor,” the strategist said.

“Overall, we believe the long-term investment case for gold remains positive,” Staunovo added. “In our view, price pullbacks toward USD 4,000/oz offer opportunities to add exposure.”

UBS’s longer-term outlook is supported by several structural factors, including central banks diversifying their reserves, concerns about rising public debt and debt-servicing costs, expectations for a weaker US dollar over time, and continued strong buying from China.

The bank continues to expect annual central bank gold purchases of between 750 and 1,000 metric tons, a source of underlying demand that could help cushion the market during periods of short-term volatility.

data.title: Lucid stock faces major risks, but a short squeeze can’t be ruled out
data.description:
Lucid Group stock has been in a strong freefall this year as the company’s future remains uncertain. It has dropped by 67% this year and by 82% in the last twelve months, with its market capitalization falling to $1.36 billion. While this sell-off may continue, the rising short interest means that it may experience a short squeeze.

Lucid Group’s short interest is rising

Lucid Group, a Saudi Arabia-backed company, has come under intense pressure this year. And at some point, there were rumors that it was considering either filing for bankruptcy or go private. In its response, the management said that it had enough liquidity to fund operations into next year. Also, it insisted that AlixPartners, its restructuring consultant, was helping it improve its operations. 

At the same time, there are signs that Saudi Arabia, its main backer, is in trouble as attacks from Houthi have escalated. Houthis have attacked several important oil targets and barred tankers from the country from passing through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The attacks have been so intense that the kingdom decided to cancel an important investment conference.

Saudi Arabia has also suffered major setbacks. Its LIV Golf investment has failed, while The Line, the futuristic city in the desert has been scaled down. As such, investors worry that the kingdom may decide to give up on Lucid, a loss-making venture.

These factors have contributed to the rising short interest, a sign that many investors expect the stock to continue falling. Its short interest has risen to 23%, the most of any American electric vehicle company. While the rising short interest is big risk, it may also expose the company to a short squeeze. 

Lucid Group’s revenue is growing, but losses are key

Lucid Group is facing major challenges. The most important one is that, while its revenue is growing, losses remain substantially high. Its last earnings report showed that its revenue rose to over $405 million in the second quarter from $259 million in the same period last year. Its half-year revenue rose to $687 million from $494 million last year.

Most of this revenue was from related parties. At the same time, the company continues to lose substantial sums of money. Its net loss in the last quarter stood at $1.03 billion, much higher than the $536 million it lost in Q2’25. 

These numbers mean that the company will continue losing money in the foreseeable future. And considering that the management expects its cash to run out next year, it means that it will need to raise cash. The challenge is that Saudi Arabia may not be interested in investing in it because of its financial position. As a result, the company may decide to raise cash by selling shares.

Lucid Group stock price technical analysis

LCID stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the LCID stock price has been in a strong sell-off for a long time, a move that has turned it into a fallen angel. Most recently, it dropped from a high of $8.50 on July 28 to the current $3.38. 

The stock has remained below the key support level of $4.46, its lowest level in June this year. It has also dropped below all moving averages. As such, the path of the least resistance for the stock is downwards, with the next target being at $2.50.

The risk for shorting the stock, however, is that it may go through a short squeeze that may push it to as high as $5.

data.title: Chipotle stock lands at a key support as top analyst slashes target: is it a buy?
data.description:
Chipotle Mexican Grill stock continued its strong downward trend as analysts remained concerned about its slowing growth. CMG dropped to $28.15, its lowest level since June 4, and 32% below the year-to-date high. Focus now shifts to the upcoming earnings report, which may shed insights on its business.

A top Chipotle Mexican Grill bull has given up

Top analysts have lowered their estimates of Chipotle Mexican Grill, citing its slow revenue and profitability growth. Andrew Charles, a TD Cowen analyst who has long maintained a bullish outlook for the stock, has downgraded his recommendation and target. 

He lowered his target from $44 to $32, the lowest target among analysts. He also noted that the stock may drop to as low as $25 a share in the next 12 months. He said:

“The start of the quarter is showing underlying softness at a time when the business ought to be clicking. Now that we believe that it’s more likely Chipotle is going to miss 2027 estimates more materially, we thought now is a good time to move to the sidelines.”

Other top analysts have lowered their targets on Chipotle stock. Deutsche Bank lowered its target from $51 to $45, while Wells Fargo’s Zachary Fadem slashed from $45 to $40. Citigroup’s John Tower cut the target from $45 to $43.

As a result, the consensus target among analysts is $43.74, much lower than where it was 12 months ago, when analysts were expecting it to rise to $56.4. 

READ MORE: Why it makes no sense for Starbucks to acquire Chipotle

Chipotle earnings will need to reassure investors

The ongoing CMG stock retreat has coincided with the weakness in its business as many consumers complain about the elevated inflation. US consumer confidence has also been in a downward trend in the past few months. 

The most recent results showed that Chipotle’s revenue rose 9.3% in the second quarter to $3.3 billion. Its comparable restaurant sales rose by 2.2%, while its operating profit margin fell to 15.7% from the previous 18.2%.

Yahoo Finance data shows that analysts expect the upcoming earnings to show that its revenue rose by 9.35% in the third quarter to $3.28 billion. Its full-year guidance is expected to come in at $13.02 billion, up by 9.2% from last year. 

Chipotle will need to reassure investors that the “Recipe for Growth” strategy was working. This approach has five pillars, including operational excellence, digital innovation, menu development, talent cultivation, and global expansion. It plans to open 350 to 370 new restaurants this year, with some of them being international ones. It has already opened new stores in Mexico.

Chipotle is also working on increasing the number of stores with Chipotlanes, improving its menu, and ways to increase traffic flow. Signs that these strategies are working will boost its stock price. 

CMG stock price technical analysis

Chipotle stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that Chipotle stock has been in a strong sell-off this year. This sell-off started in 2024 when it peaked at $69.28. It has formed a series of lower lows and lower highs. 

The stock has dropped below all moving averages. It is also stuck at a crucial support level, which coincides with the lowest level in June. 

Moving below that level will point to more downside, potentially to the psychological level of $25, which is about 10% below the current level.

data.title: Dow opens 500 points lower as oil prices rise and tech stocks face renewed pressure
data.description:
US stocks edged lower on Friday as investors remained cautious following a sharp sell-off in technology stocks, while rising oil prices and concerns about renewed conflict in the Middle East added to market uncertainty.

The S&P 500 fell 0.51%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 536 points.

The Nasdaq Composite declined 0.41%, signalling further pressure on technology shares after the Nasdaq Composite lost nearly 3% on Thursday.

Telecommunications stocks also came under pressure after reports that SpaceX was in discussions with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a nationwide wireless carrier programme.

Meanwhile, rising crude prices renewed concerns about inflation ahead of next week's Federal Reserve policy meeting.

Telecom stocks fall as SpaceX explores wireless expansion

AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile fell between 2% and 4% in trading following reports of SpaceX's potential expansion into the US wireless market.

The development raised concerns about increased competition for established telecommunications providers.

The news had the opposite effect on cell tower operators. Crown Castle shares rose 13.6%, while American Tower gained 6.99%.

Technology stocks remained under pressure after Thursday's sell-off, when Meta Platforms fell nearly 8% following its quarterly results.

The company reported its first cash outflow in more than a decade, intensifying concerns about the financial impact of its artificial intelligence investments.

CoreWeave, which has faced scrutiny over its debt burden and the cost of financing AI infrastructure, declined another 1.46% in trading on Friday. Microsoft and Meta shares were also slightly lower.

The latest weakness followed a brief recovery on Wednesday, when upbeat results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer helped lift AI-related shares.

Chipmakers Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices were showing modest gains.

Investors are also looking ahead to earnings from Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon next week, with results expected to provide further insight into technology spending and demand for AI infrastructure.

Oil prices rise as Middle East risks fuel inflation concerns

Oil prices continued to climb on Friday as concerns about potential disruptions to Middle Eastern supplies supported crude markets.

US West Texas Intermediate futures rose 1.89% to $101.35 a barrel, while Brent crude gained 1.59% to $114.94.

The increases followed reports that the US and Israel were considering plans for renewed attacks on Iran amid the regional conflict that began in late February.

Higher energy prices added to inflation concerns ahead of the Federal Reserve's meeting next week.

Markets broadly expect the central bank to leave interest rates unchanged, while expectations of a rate hike this month have declined following comments from officials suggesting there is little urgency to tighten policy.

The 10-year US Treasury yield rose one basis point to 4.968% on Friday after falling sharply in the previous session as investors sought the relative safety of government bonds.

The 30-year yield was flat, while the two-year yield declined two basis points.

Earnings outlook improves as investors assess market volatility

Despite the recent technology sell-off, forecasts for corporate earnings have strengthened.

Growth in third-quarter S&P 500 profits is now projected at 32.3%, up from the previous estimate of 30.7%, according to LSEG data.

Other movers included American Express, which fell 2.2% despite raising its 2026 profit forecast after reporting strong third-quarter results.

Oilfield services provider SLB gained 1.3% after beating analysts' profit estimates.

Gold miner Newmont dropped 1.18% after reporting quarterly results and warning that unit costs were expected to rise in 2027.

Bloom Energy declined 10% despite raising its fiscal 2026 forecast.

For the week, the Nasdaq was on track to lose 0.5%, while the S&P 500 was heading for a gain of less than 0.1%.

The Dow was positioned for a 1.7% advance, supported by defensive sectors as investors sought to limit exposure to technology-market volatility.

data.title: 10-year Treasury yield holds below 5% as AI debt and oil risks weigh
data.description:
US Treasury yields edged higher early Friday after a sharp decline in the previous session.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield rose 2 basis points to 4.9779%, while the two-year yield increased by the same amount to 4.6647%.

The 30-year yield climbed more than 1 basis point to 5.3007%.

The moves followed a substantial rally in government bonds on Thursday, when investors sought safe-haven assets amid concerns about AI-related borrowing and geopolitical risks.

The 10-year yield fell 17 basis points to 4.972%, its largest single-day decline since March 10, 2023, and its first move below 5% in a month.

"Yesterday, the yield on the US 10-year note dropped 17 basis points taking it back below 5.0% for the first time in a month. Given the selloff across US tech, the bond market rally looks like a flight to safety," David Morrison, Senior Market Analyst at Trade Nation said in an emailed commentary.

Bond prices move inversely to yields, meaning the previous session’s decline reflected strong demand for US government debt.

Bank of America expects further declines

Bank of America strategists led by Michael Hartnett said they remained “tactically risk-off” until mid-November, anticipating further declines in stocks, Treasury yields and the US dollar before markets find a floor.

The strategists expect the 30-year Treasury yield to move toward 5% and the dollar index to fall below 100.

They identified three developments that could help bring the current market weakness to an end: markets fully pricing in a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections, the European Central Bank and French government halting the selloff in French bonds, and an indication that AI-related borrowing has peaked.

The last condition could come through a reduction in capital expenditure by large technology companies or an extreme equity issuance announcement that signals a peak in spreads on hyperscaler debt.

The comments highlight how concerns over the financing of AI infrastructure have become a growing source of uncertainty for financial markets, alongside persistent inflation and geopolitical tensions.

Oil prices add to inflation concerns

Energy prices remained another source of pressure as fresh attacks by Iran-backed Houthi militants against Saudi Arabian facilities heightened concerns about potential supply disruptions.

West Texas Intermediate crude futures for December delivery rose 1.16% to $100.61 a barrel, while Brent crude, the international benchmark, gained 0.79% to $114.06.

The latest gains followed reports earlier this week suggesting that the US and Israel could resume strikes against Iran after the November midterm elections.

Higher oil prices threaten to keep inflation elevated, potentially complicating the Federal Reserve’s efforts to bring price growth back toward its 2% target.

Persistent energy-driven inflation could also limit the central bank’s flexibility to ease monetary policy.

The combination of rising energy costs and concerns about government borrowing has helped keep longer-dated Treasury yields elevated, even as demand for safe-haven assets produced Thursday’s sharp decline.

Fed decision and PMI data in focus

Investors are also preparing for the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision next week.

Friday’s flash S&P Global purchasing managers’ index readings for manufacturing and services could offer fresh clues about the strength of US economic activity and the direction of inflation pressures.

The data arrive at a sensitive point for markets, with investors balancing the possibility of tighter monetary policy against signs of growing caution around AI investment and geopolitical risks.

The 10-year yield’s move below 5% on Thursday offered some relief after a period of heavy selling in government bonds.

However, the modest rebound on Friday suggests that investors remain cautious about the outlook for inflation and interest rates.

data.title: Top DAX Index shares to watch next week: Deutsche Bank, BASF, Mercedes
data.description:
The DAX Index has come under pressure over the past few months. After peaking at 26,630 points in August, it has dropped to its current level of 25,150. The retreat coincided with weakness in European equities and rising crude oil prices. This article highlights some of the top German stocks to watch next week.

Deutsche Bank

Deutsche Bank, like other European banks, has come into a bear market this year. It has plunged from a high of €35.85 in September to the current €27.67, its lowest level since June 12. 

The retreat has happened as investors book profits in European banks. Also, the investment banking industry has gone through a significant slowdown in the second half of the year as interest rates have soared. 

The most recent results showed that Deutsche Bank’s revenue rose by 9% to €8.5 billion, while its profit soared by 10% to €1.9 billion. Most notably, the company’s return on tangible equity rose to 11%. The upcoming earnings will provide more color on its business and the outlook for the year.

BASF 

BASF, a top chemicals company, will be in the spotlight as it publishes its financial results. These numbers come at a time when its stock is in a recovery mode. It jumped from a low of €46 in July to the current €52.79. 

The upcoming results will be important as the company is in talks to acquire Evonik, a company that makes 100s of chemicals. Evonik has already rejected the $11.7 billion offer, noting that it undervalued the company. 

BASF is still interested in Evonik, with management hinting that it may hike the offer to $12.9 billion. Evonik, on the other hand, is considering buying Ashland, an American company. 

The most recent numbers showed that BASF’s sales jumped to €17.2 billion in the first half of the year. Its EBITDA jumped by 48% to €1.96 billion, with the net income hitting €4.1 billion.

Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, and Volkswagen

German automakers will be in the spotlight next week as they publish their earnings. These results come at a time when these companies are going through a big challenge, which explains why the stocks have dropped. 

Mercedes-Benz stock has dropped by over 33% from its highest point this year. Porsche has dropped by 16% from the year-to-date high, while Volkswagen is down by over 32% from its peak last year. VW is hovering near its lowest level in decades. 

The three companies have made some major announcements lately. Volkswagen is considering large layoffs to reduce its costs and boost profitability. Porsche, on the other hand, is focusing on becoming a more premium brand by focusing on value over volume. It is also working on building the sportiest vehicle in every segment. It also lowered its breakeven point to below 200k vehicles. 

These developments come at a time when European companies are facing challenges in the Chinese market, where they had a big market share. Today, many Chinese brands like BYD, Nio, and Xiaomi are gaining market share. 

Other top DAX companies will publish their earnings next week, including Linde, MTU Aero, Covestro, and Beiersdorf.

data.title: Cardano rebounds toward $0.216 amid whale selling and falling OI
data.description:
Cardano edged higher on Friday, trading around $0.2156 after a roughly 6% decline in the previous session.

The nearly 2% rebound offered some relief, but ADA remained below key moving averages and its former rising support trendline.

Mixed whale activity and weaker derivatives positioning suggest the recovery still faces selling pressure.

Momentum indicators also remained subdued, leaving the $0.20 psychological level in focus if sellers regain control.

Large wallet holdings show mixed trends

Santiment data showed that wallets holding between 10 million and 100 million ADA controlled 37.93% of circulating supply on Friday, down from 38.27% on October 10.

The decline indicates reduced holdings within that cohort, although changes in wallet classifications can also affect these measures.

The largest holders moved in the opposite direction. Wallets holding more than 100 million ADA increased their share to 16.04%, from 15.92% over the same period.

The figures therefore show uneven positioning among large investors rather than uniform selling across all whale groups.

Meanwhile, the proportion of ADA supply in profit fell to 17.8%, from 30.78%.

That means fewer tokens were trading above their acquisition cost. 

The metric alone does not establish that holders realized profits, as falling prices can also push previously profitable holdings into losses.

CoinGlass data showed Cardano futures open interest declining 3.3% over 24 hours to $467.97 million.

Falling open interest alongside the recent price decline is consistent with positions being closed and leverage leaving the market.

Because open interest is measured in dollars, lower token prices can also reduce its reported value.

Liquidations totaled approximately $1.08 million, including $1.02 million in longs, showing that bullish leveraged traders absorbed nearly all forced closures.

However, the funding rate remains positive at 0.0038%. Positive funding means long-position holders pay shorts, reflecting a bullish tilt in perpetual futures positioning.

Together, the readings suggest mixed reaction among traders despite Friday’s modest price recovery.

Cardano technical outlook: ADA faces support test at $0.20

Cardano’s daily chart remains bearish below the 50-day Exponential Moving Average at $0.2274 and the broken rising trendline around $0.2282.

These levels form a nearby resistance zone, while the 200-day EMA at $0.2322 presents a higher barrier.

The Relative Strength Index sits near 41, indicating weak momentum below the neutral threshold.

The MACD is declining into negative territory, reinforcing the cautious outlook.

On the downside, immediate support lies at the $0.2000 round figure.

A sustained break below that level would bring the August 30 low at $0.1894 into focus.

For the recovery to strengthen, ADA would first need to overcome the $0.2274–$0.2282 resistance band.

A sustained daily close above the 200-day EMA at $0.2322 would further weaken the bearish setup and improve prospects for a broader rebound.

Until those barriers are reclaimed, Friday’s advance remains a modest recovery within a corrective trend.

data.title: Anthropic set to launch AI consultancy services in Europe: report
data.description:
Anthropic is expanding its enterprise AI business through a new partnership with London-based private equity firm Hg.

The tech giant seeks to help European companies integrate artificial intelligence into their operations ahead of a closely watched stock market debut.

According to the Financial Times, the two companies are setting up an independent consultancy that will place AI consultants and engineers within businesses to accelerate the adoption of the technology.

The venture is expected to begin operations by the end of 2026, with London and Berlin serving as its main hubs.

The partnership marks Anthropic's first standalone consultancy venture in Europe.

How the Anthropic-Hg partnership will work

The new company will help businesses incorporate AI into their existing workflows and develop new products using the technology.

Rather than limiting its role to supplying AI models, Anthropic is seeking to bring technical expertise directly into organizations to help turn AI capabilities into practical business applications.

The IPO bound company will contribute capital from its balance sheet, while Hg will invest through the funds it manages.

The arrangement combines Anthropic's AI technology and engineering capabilities with Hg's experience investing in software and services businesses.

The venture also creates a potential channel for deploying AI across companies backed by Hg, building on the firm's existing efforts to introduce AI tools throughout its portfolio.

Anthropic takes aim at traditional consultancies

The move adds to growing competition between AI developers and established IT consulting firms.

Traditional consultancies have helped businesses integrate new technologies, but AI companies are increasingly building their own implementation services to guide customers from experimentation to operational deployment.

Anthropic has already entered the sector in the United States through Ode, an independent AI services company introduced in July.

Backed by Blackstone and Hellman & Friedman, along with investors including Goldman Sachs, Apollo Global Management, General Atlantic and others, Ode combines Anthropic's AI models with experienced engineers to help businesses identify and implement AI applications.

Rival OpenAI is pursuing a similar strategy.

In May, it launched the OpenAI Deployment Company to help businesses build and integrate AI systems into their core operations, extending its reach beyond the development and sale of AI models.

European expansion comes ahead of major IPO

Anthropic's consulting push comes as it prepares for a potential initial public offering that could test investor appetite for AI companies amid questions about valuations and the cost of developing advanced models.

The company could make its IPO prospectus public as soon as Friday, October 23, according to media reports.

Anthropic is targeting a potential November listing, although the reported timeline remains subject to change.

Investor expectations have also shifted. Some prospective and existing investors are reportedly considering a valuation of around $1.5 trillion, below the roughly $2 trillion figure discussed previously.

The reassessment follows fresh disclosures about the company's financial performance and the substantial costs associated with AI development.

A draft IPO prospectus reportedly showed that Anthropic recorded a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, compared with $13 billion a year earlier.

However, approximately $72 billion of the reported loss came from a non-cash accounting charge related to an increase in the estimated value of convertible bonds and other financing instruments, rather than operating expenses.
